national_articles.headline: FAQs outline automated 90% GST refunds and shorter processing deadlines
national_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) is introducing a phased, fully automated refund processing system, following approval from the GST Council, to speed up working capital release for businesses, enabling automated 90 percent provisional refunds on low-risk claims without tax officer intervention and cutting acknowledgement timelines from 15 to 10 days. The CBIC has issued the following FAQs to explain the new changes: Q. What are the key changes being introduced in the refund mechanism? The existing refund mechanism is being modified to provide for time-bound and automated processing of refund claims in specified categories on the basis of risk analysis by the system, so as to enhance ease of doing business, improve transparency and expedite the processing of refund claims to ease the working capital requirement of the taxpayers. The changes are being introduced in 2 phases as per readiness of the system. Phase I:There shall be reduction of time limit for acknowledgement or deficiency memo from 15 to 10 days, and in case, no action is taken by the officer in 10 days, the application will be deemed to be acknowledged and the acknowledgement will be given by the system. There will be automated sanctioning of provisional refund, to the extent of 90% of the refund amount claimed, by the system for acknowledged low-risk refund claims pertaining to zero-rated supplies or inverted duty structure. There will be automated sanctioning of final refund by the system in case of refund claim on account of any balance in electronic cash ledger. Phase II:Auto acknowledgement of refund application shall be done by the system after validation of information in the refund application. In case of any mismatch, the system would communicate the error(s) to the taxpayer for rectification of the errors and filing of a fresh application. However, in case the validation failure reoccurs, the application may be forwarded to the proper officer for scrutiny and processing. Further, in case of low-risk zero-rated supply refund claims, final refund shall also be automatically given by the system. Q. Which categories of refund are eligible for automated provisional refund? Refund of unutilized ITC for low-risk refund claims pertaining to zero-rated supplies or inverted duty structure are eligible for automated provisional refund. Q. How does automated provisional refund differ from the earlier provisional refund process? In case of low-risk refund claims on account of zero-rated supplies and inverted duty structure, after the issuance of acknowledgement, 90% of the claimed amount will be sanctioned provisionally by the system on an automated basis, without the intervention of tax officer. Q. Are there any exclusions to sanction of provisional refund in respect of refund claims on account of zero-rated supplies and inverted duty structure? Certain notified categories of persons engaged in the supply of commodities such as areca nuts, pan masala, tobacco and manufactured tobacco substitutes, essential oils are not eligible for refund on provisional basis. Any person, who has not undergone Aadhaar authentication under rule 10B of the CGST Rules, 2017, shall also not be eligible for refund on a provisional basis. Kindly refer to notification No. 14/2025–Central Tax dated 17.09.2025 for more details. Q. What will be the role of officer in the processing of refund application? In Phase I, the officer shall issue acknowledgement within 10 days of receipt of application after checking for its completeness. In case he finds any discrepancy in the documents, a deficiency memo may be issued to the claimant intimating such deficiency. While the provisional refund in the acknowledged cases will be sanctioned by the system in cases involving low risk zero-rated supplies and inverted duty structure, the final processing and scrutiny of refund will be done by the proper officer. Further, in cases where the refund claim is not eligible for provisional refund, the processing and scrutiny of refund applications shall be done by the proper officer. In Phase II, the following cases will be handled by the proper officer: processing of refund claims which are not identified by the system for processing on an automated route. Final scrutiny of refund claims in case of inverted duty structure refunds, after provisional refund to the extent of 90 percent of the claimed amount is sanctioned by the system. Q. Can the proper officer deny provisional refund even if a refund application is low‑risk? In case of low-risk refund applications on account of zero-rated supply and inverted duty structure, the system will automatically sanction 90% of the claimed amount on a provisional basis. This will be fully system- driven and there will be no officer interface at this stage. Q. Will the new form increase my compliance burden?  No, the updated refund form does not increase compliance burden. Information that was hitherto required to be uploaded in scanned form will now be captured within the application itself, enabling system-based data matching. This makes the refund process more predictable, smooth, and transparent, thereby benefitting the taxpayer.

national_articles.headline: Waterways Leisure Tourism Q2 results: Cordelia Cruises operator swings to Rs 58 crore net profit
national_articles.body: Waterways Leisure Tourism, operator of Cordelia Cruises, on Friday reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 58.49 crore for the September quarter of the current fiscal, compared with a loss of Rs 8.9 crore in the year-ago period. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 23 crore in the April-June quarter of FY27. Revenue from operations rose over 30 percent to Rs 133 crore in the July-September quarter, from Rs 102 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal. EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) turned positive at Rs 9.7 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 6.5 crore a year earlier. The September quarter's profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 49.5 crore recorded by its subsidiary Bay Cruise Investments Inc. as compensation received without obligation for the early delivery of the vessel Sky. The vessel arrived on September 10, ahead of its originally scheduled delivery date of September 30. For the six months ended September 30, the company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 81.3 crore, compared with Rs 25.8 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue for the period rose to Rs 323 crore from Rs 277.9 crore. Waterways Leisure Tourismwas listed on the BSE and NSE on July 1, following its initial public offering (IPO). The company's board had approved a sub-division of its equity shares on July 10, splitting each share with a face value of Rs 10 into 10 shares of Re 1 each. Shareholders subsequently approved the proposal through a postal ballot on August 12. Shares of the company settled 1.87 percent lower at Rs 100.98 per share on the NSE on Friday. national_articles.headline: States to get new measure of household consumption, private investment as MoSPI revamps GDP framework
national_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links India is moving towards a new framework to measure household consumption and private investment at the state level, with the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) outlining a methodology that could provide a clearer picture of the drivers of economic growth across states. The guidelines propose estimating Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) through the expenditure approach. Unlike the production approach, which measures economic activity through value added across industries, the expenditure approach captures spending by households, governments and businesses, along with exports and imports. The proposed framework could help policymakers assess whether economic activity in a state is being driven by household consumption, government spending or investment, rather than relying solely on the contribution of different industries. Household surveys to drive consumption estimates One of the key changes proposed is the use of the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) to estimate Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) across states. Under the proposed methodology, state-wise per capita household expenditure from the HCES will be combined with population projections to derive the shares used to distribute national consumption estimates across states. The methodology also proposes greater use of household surveys for estimating consumption at the national level. Vehicle sales, electricity and banking data to track spending For consumption categories where household survey data are insufficient, MoSPI has proposed using administrative data to estimate state-wise expenditure. Electricity consumption will be allocated using domestic electricity sales reported by the Central Electricity Authority, while LPG and kerosene consumption will be estimated using state-level data from the petroleum ministry. Purchases of cars and motorcycles will be estimated using sale-price data from the Vahan portal. The number of registered vehicles, assuming an average lifespan of 15 years, will also be used to allocate expenditure on vehicle maintenance, fuel and road transport services. Banking and insurance expenditure will be estimated using Reserve Bank of India data on deposits and personalloans,along with insurance premiums reported by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. Similarly, air passenger traffic and telecom subscriptions will help estimate expenditure on air travel and communication services across states. New methodology to estimate private investment The guidelines also propose changes to the measurement of private corporate investment across states, particularly in industries where direct capital expenditure data are unavailable. MoSPI has recommended using national capital-output ratios alongside state-level Gross Value Added (GVA) to estimate capital stock and investment.  The ministry has also recommended deferring the compilation of state-level imports and exports of goods and services until relevant data become available.

national_articles.headline: Jio Platforms sets IPO price band at Rs 1,065-1,119 per share: Report
national_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links Jio Platforms Ltd. is set to price its shares at 1,065 rupees to 1,119 rupees apiece in its planned initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter. The company is targeting a market value of as much as 10.3 trillion rupees ($107 billion), the people said, asking not to be identified because the information isn’t yet public. At the upper end of the price band, Jio’s IPO would raise about 302 billion rupees, according to Bloomberg calculations. That would keep it on track to become India’s largest-ever IPO. The telecom and digital services arm of Reliance Industries Ltd. plans to open public subscription on Oct. 21 and close it two days later, the people said. The anchor book is scheduled to open on Oct. 19, with the shares expected to begin trading on Oct. 28, they said. Deliberations are ongoing and details including the price range, valuation and timing could still change, the people said. A Reliance Industries representative did not offer any immediate comments. The valuation falls short of some earlier expectations, though the offering is still poised to surpass Hyundai Motor India Ltd.’s 278 billion-rupee share sale in October 2024, the country’s biggest. That will be a major test of investor appetite for large share sales in one of the world’s busiest markets for equity fundraising. Jio filed its draft prospectus in June for an offering of as many as 270 million new shares, equivalent to about 2.93% of its post-issue equity capital, according to Bloomberg calculations. The company was earlier poised to seek a valuation of about 11 trillion rupees, people familiar with the matter have said. Valuations floated earlier were even higher, in the range of $130 billion to $170 billion at one point. A selloff in Indian stocks has since tempered pricing expectations for several IPOs in the country. In June, local brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services estimated Jio’s valuation at between $115 billion and $118 billion, while Dolat Capital valued the company at about $110 billion. Jio has appointed 19 banks to work on the share sale, including Kotak Mahindra Capital Co., Morgan Stanley, Bank of America Corp., Axis Capital Ltd., BNP Paribas SA and Citigroup Inc.

international_articles.headline: US Embassy in Jordan warns Americans of attacks, travel disruptions
international_articles.body: The US Embassy in Jordan on Friday urged American citizens across the Middle East to exercise heightened caution, warning of possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and threats to US interests amid hostilities involving Iran-backed Houthi forces and Saudi Arabia. “Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment,” the embassy said in a statement posted on X, warning that the situation could escalate rapidly. The advisory asked American citizens to be aware of potential travel disruptions, including flight cancellations and airspace closures, as regional hostilities continue. The embassy said Iranian-supported Houthi forces had engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure that resulted in civilian casualties. It also warned that Iran and its allies could target American interests beyond the immediate conflict zone. Iran and its allies “may target other US interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including US businesses and other institutions”, the embassy said. The warning extended to locations associated with American citizens and institutions worldwide, including US businesses. The US Embassy urged American citizens to monitor updates from the Jordanian government about specific threats and follow official instructions, including sirens and other warnings.  It also advised citizens to keep track of US embassy travel advisories and guidance for the latest security information.

international_articles.headline: 'I may share this with Trump': Navi Pillay quips after winning Nobel Peace Prize | Video
international_articles.body: South African champion of international law Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year's Nobel Peace Prize, joked that she might "share the prize" with US President Donald Trump if people kept applauding her. "If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," Pillay said in a video posted to X by the Secretary General of Amnesty International, which showed Pillay being applauded in Nuremberg after the announcement of the award.  — Insider Paper (@TheInsiderPaper)October 9, 2026 She said that her first reaction to hearing the news was that it must be a joke. "Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this," the 85-year-old said, wanting to make sure it was true. Pillay mentioned her work heading the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza. "The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what's happening there as genocide," she said. "One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was, why would you need courage to speak the truth?" she added. Sharif's pitch for Trump Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif once again made a public pitch for US PresidentDonald Trumpto receive the Nobel Peace Prize, crediting him with preventing a wider conflict between India and Pakistan in May 2025. The appeal came shortly before the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South African jurist of Indian origin Navanethem “Navi” Pillay. In a post on X, Sharif praised Trump’s role in South Asia and said Pakistan had nominated the US president for the award. The Pakistani prime minister also expressed hope that Trump’s efforts to promote peace and prevent conflict would receive recognition “this time”. Trump's appeal for peace prize Trump has long coveted the prize and has made no secret of his aspiration to win it. He has previously heaped pressure on the Norwegian Committee to give him the prestigious accolade. “I’ve done stuff that nobody else has ever done. I’m not bragging, I’m just telling you the facts,” the president told reporters on Wednesday. “No president has probably ever settled any wars. I settled eight wars." The White House reacted furiously to Trump’s snub last year and accused the Committee of placing “politics over peace” when the prize was awarded to Venezuela's Maria Corina Machado, a democracy and peace activist challenged Venezuela’s autocratic government.  She later symbolically handed her prize to Trump as a “recognition for his unique commitment with our freedom”.

international_articles.headline: Iranian ships run low on food and fuel as Sri Lanka weighs aid amid US sanctions risk
international_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links Sri Lanka has no immediate plans to assist 19 Iranian ships anchored in international waters off its coast, despite reported shortages of food, fresh water and fuel. Colombo is weighing humanitarian concerns against the risk of US secondary sanctions. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Thushara Rodrigo said the vessels were anchored about 24 nautical miles from Sri Lanka’s coast and had reported shortages of essential supplies. He said the government would prioritise national interests before considering assistance and that companies supplying the ships were aware of the potential sanctions risks. Rodrigo added that Sri Lanka had received no communication from Washington warning of repercussions if it decided to help. The Iranian Embassy in Colombo said it had no details on the matter. The US embassy in Colombo had informed the Sri Lankan government in August that it was tracking 19 Iranian oil tankers off the country’s western coast and urged officials to tell local port service providers to deny the vessels support or risk US secondary sanctions, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing Sri Lankan government documents and accounts from shipping companies. Herath has denied that Washington pressured Colombo to withhold assistance. The reported restrictions have made it difficult for the crews to obtain essential supplies. Shipping agents based in Dubai appealed to Sri Lankan businesses to send food and fuel, but local companies said obtaining approval for supply visits had become difficult, according to the Wall Street Journal report. The newspaper also reported that the Sri Lanka Ports Authority considered it unwise to provide services to Iranian-flagged vessels because of the sanctions risk. A Sri Lankan ship repair company that sent workers aboard one Iranian vessel shortly before the restrictions took effect found that provisions were running low. The crew asked the workers to bring their own food and said they could not wash because the ship needed to conserve fresh water, the report said. Another shipper received urgent requests for food and provisions from agents representing the tankers. US blockade leaves Iranian vessels stranded Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath told the local Sunday Times newspaper that the vessels were Iranian oil tankers that had been anchored off Sri Lanka for several months after the US resumed its naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving Iranian ships unable to return home. Before the disruption, Iranian crude was transported to international waters off Malaysia and transferred between tankers before being shipped to Chinese refineries, a route used to circumvent US sanctions on Iranian oil exports. The blockade has disrupted this trade, while Asian ports have become reluctant to service Iranian vessels for fear of sanctions. Container ships carrying goods such as corn and industrial materials to Iran have also been affected. The US embassy in Colombo held a three-day session in mid-September with more than 40 Sri Lankan officials to explain the sanctions risks associated with providing services to sanctioned vessels, according to the Wall Street Journal report. The situation puts Colombo in a difficult position as it recovers from an economic crisis and seeks to maintain ties with both Washington and Tehran. The US played an important role in supporting Sri Lanka’s International Monetary Fund bailout and helping its agricultural sector avert a food crisis, while Iran is also an important trading partner. The dilemma follows Sri Lanka’s earlier assistance to Iranian sailors after a US torpedo attack sank the naval ship IRIS Dena nearly seven months ago, killing 87 sailors. The vessel was returning from a naval exercise at India’s invitation. Sri Lanka treated wounded sailors and repatriated them, including those rescued from a second Iranian ship that had reported technical problems. International affairs analyst Dayan Jayatilleka said Sri Lanka faced practical limits on what it could do, but had a moral obligation to assist vessels in certain circumstances.  “These are not warships. These are cargo ships which carried oil to China from Iran,” Jayatilleka said. He added that if the vessels entered Sri Lankan waters because they were under attack, Sri Lanka would have a moral obligation to assist them immediately.

international_articles.headline: Pakistan has ‘substantial’ forces in Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
international_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links Pakistan has a “substantial” number of troops deployed in Saudi Arabia in a defensive capacity as the kingdom faces repeated attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi militants, Pakistan’s foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday. “From Pakistan already we have substantial number of forces as well as resources in town, in Riyadh,” Khan told journalists, adding that Pakistani military personnel would not cross into the territory of the other side to attack the Houthis but would act in defence of Saudi territory. Khan declined to say whether fresh Pakistani deployments had been made since the conflict intensified. He said decisions on “how much and when and where” forces would be deployed would be up to the trilateral alliance, which is headquartered in Riyadh and has a retired Pakistani general as its secretary general. Pakistan’s military spokesperson, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, also confirmed that Pakistani forces were stationed in the kingdom, saying they had maintained a presence there for decades and operated across “multiple capabilities and domains”. “I can confirm that we, the forces of Pakistan, are already there [in the Kingdom]. That I can assure you,” Chaudhry said in an interview with CNN. The statements come as Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye coordinate under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in the Saudi holy city on August 7, 2026. The pact commits the three countries to treat an armed attack against one member as an attack against all. At a meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defense Committee of the Makkah Alliance for Defense in Riyadh on October 5, officials from the three countries condemned attacks and threats against Saudi Arabia’s security and territorial integrity. They pledged to provide designated military forces and capabilities for rapid deployment in accordance with each country’s national legislation. However, the countries have not disclosed the number of troops involved, their missions, command arrangements, costs or the duration of the deployment. It remains unclear whether Pakistan will send additional personnel under the trilateral agreement or whether troops already stationed in Saudi Arabia will participate directly in military operations against the Houthis. According to Reuters, Pakistan’s information ministry said the alliance had completed the necessary government procedures but did not clarify whether the cabinet or parliament had been involved. It described details of the deployment as a matter of operational confidentiality. The agreement follows a separate bilateral defence pact signed by Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in September 2025. Under that arrangement, Islamabad deployed about 8,000 troops, a squadron of fighter jets and an air defence system to the kingdom, Reuters reported in May. Khan said Pakistani forces had been deployed in Saudi Arabia regularly since the 1980s. Turkiye is also assessing how it can help Saudi Arabia counter Houthi attacks under the trilateral agreement, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday, according to Reuters. Fidan described the pact as defensive rather than offensive and said officials were examining possible contributions, particularly in air defence. He added that preparations to submit the agreement to the Turkish parliament for ratification had been completed. Separately, Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing two officials, that Turkiye was providing mainly defensive and technical support to Saudi Arabia. The precise scope of the assistance was not disclosed. The developments come amid repeated Houthi attacks involving drones and missiles targeting Saudi civilian and economic infrastructure. The Houthis announced a ban on Saudi shipping in July and have since attacked tankers and oil facilities. The Houthis also launched aerial attacks on Saudi targets, including Riyadh’s international airport on Thursday, killing three, according to the additional report. The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen separately said the group had struck a power station in Medina that supplies electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque. The Houthis denied the allegation. Pakistan’s potential military role also carries diplomatic implications. Islamabad is engaged in diplomatic efforts involving Iran as a mediator in the US-led war on Iran. Direct military involvement against the Houthis, who are backed by Tehran, could strain Pakistan’s relations with Iran. The deployment has also raised questions about the Pakistani military’s influence over the country’s foreign and defence policy under Field Marshal Asim Munir. The arrangement marks a contrast with 2015, when Saudi Arabia requested Pakistani troops, aircraft and naval vessels for its campaign in Yemen. Pakistan’s government referred the request to parliament, which voted unanimously to maintain neutrality while pledging to protect Saudi territory and the holy sites. According to Reuters, analysts say the difference between the two episodes is political rather than legal. Pakistan’s Constitution placed control and command of the armed forces with the federal government in 2015, as it does today. Constitutional amendments passed last year placed Munir in charge of all three military services until 2030. He was also granted the rank of field marshal for life and immunity from criminal prosecution. The developments come amid domestic political tensions involving supporters of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, who have accused the military of excessive influence over politics. The army has denied the allegation. Zulfi Bukhari, a spokesperson for Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party, did not say whether the party supported the deployment but told Reuters that the issue should be debated and decided with “political acumen”. Andreas Krieg, an associate professor at King’s College London, told Reuters that foreign partners’ reliance on Pakistan’s military could reinforce its domestic position.  Partners “do not create Pakistan’s civil-military imbalance, but they can reward it,” Krieg said, adding that a system with weak counterweights was “good at entering commitments and worse at correcting them once costs emerge”.
